title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
abstract: Majorana drew a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the Bloch sphere, antipodal to the zeros of its overlap with spin coherent states. Projecting only one qubit of a general state leaves the others in a state that varies with direction. Its entanglement invariants are eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix and form bands over the sphere. Exceptional points appear, without gain or loss, where the entanglement family of the rest changes. Circling one exchanges two bands, so the bands form one Riemann surface. At five qubits it fixes the entanglement class up to finitely many choices.
summary: This theoretical work develops an 'entanglement band structure' to classify general multiqubit quantum states. It shows that by projecting one qubit, the entanglement invariants form bands whose topology is encoded in a spectral curve $C$. This curve's genus and the behavior around exceptional points provide deep, geometric invariants for the state's entanglement class.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the entanglement structure of general multiqubit states by extending Majorana's construction to analyze conditional states resulting from projecting only one qubit.
main_result: The entanglement invariants form 'entanglement bands' whose structure is governed by a spectral curve $C$ with a genus determined by the number of qubits, and these bands exhibit predictable topological behavior around exceptional points.
method: The analysis involves defining entanglement invariants as eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix $L(u)$ derived from the conditional state. The structure is then mapped onto a spectral curve $C$ in complex geometry.
model_or_system: The system under study is general multiqubit states ($\Psi$), with specific focus on five-qubit systems. The analysis centers on the conditional state remaining after projecting one qubit onto a specific basis state.
key_observables: Entanglement invariants (eigenvalues of $L(u)$), Exceptional Points (EPs), the spectral curve $C$, and its genus ($g$).
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($N$), the projection direction on the Bloch sphere, and the topological winding number around EPs.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the conditional state belongs to a generic family ($	ext{Gabcd}$) and relies on algebraic structures derived from the matrix $L(u)$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entanglement bands over the Bloch sphere, the structure near an EP, the resulting braid structure forming a Riemann surface, and the locations of the EPs.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mathematical framework by defining the band structure via $L(u)$, analyzing its topological properties (Riemann surface, genus), and comparing the resulting spectral curve $C$ to known invariants of the state class.
why_interesting: The use of spectral curves and topological invariants (genus, Riemann surfaces) to classify quantum states provides a powerful, geometry-based tool for understanding entanglement beyond simple measures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Entanglement bands of the state Ψ0 of the Supplemental Material [22], with the fifth qubit projected and the split 12|34. (a) Real parts of the four bands along the great circle of real t, divided by 1 + t2. No exceptional point lies on this circle, so every crossing is one of real parts only. (b) Near an exceptional point t0, where two bands meet at w0, they form a square-root sheet, with t −t0 in units of the disc radius. (c) Around a loop enclosing all exceptional points the bands braid with 24 crossings of one sign, the (4, 8) torus link, shown after a radial rescaling that leaves the braid unchanged. (d) The 24 exceptional points on the Bloch sphere.

FIG. 2. Real parts of the bands along real t, without the division by 1 + t2 of Fig. 1(a), for a generic five-qubit state and for the GHZ, W and Dicke states. The generic bands braid into one surface, while the curves of the named states fall apart into copies of the sphere.
